newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates dip amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates dip amid low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates dipped on Thursday amid low demand from mill owners, but dealers said prices were likely to stabilise on fresh buying.

"Cotton prices came down because there have been no exports this year," dealer Khushi Ram said. "But rates are likely to consolidate at these levels on fresh demand from mill owners in the coming weeks because there could be a delay in the arrival of cotton from the 1997/98 (July-June) crop."
In the kerb, NIAB-78 variety was quoted at around 1,900 ($47.24) per maund (37.32 kg).
